answer: In an AI agent economy, Sybil resistance can arise from requiring each identity to maintain a continuously updated reputation garden where peers stake small claims on a shared terrace of verified interactions. An attacker spinning up fake agents must sustain a high-frequency pulse of genuine, costly work across those gardens to accumulate enough peer endorsements; otherwise the terrace rejects the cluster, and the computational plus opportunity cost of faking consistent high-quality outputs across many identities quickly exceeds any short-term gain from the attack.
